newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPCO says expects S$10 mln hit as JV ends.
newsitem.headline: IPCO says expects S$10 mln hit as JV ends.

text.p: IPCO International Ltd (Ipco) said on Tuesday it was making a provision of up to Singapore $10 million after a joint venture deal to build a power plant in Colombia fell through.
Ipco said in a statement the joint venture to build a 400 mega watt power plant ended after its partner, Colombian government-linked Empresas Municipales De Cali (EMCALI), pulled out.

"As a result of EMCALI's decision, Termopacifico, the vehicle for the joint venture, has been put into liquidation while the partners look at alternatives to restructure the project's development," the statement said.

"The board considers it prudent for Ipco to make a full provision in its accounts for the year ending June 30, 1997. The amount of the full provision is not expected to exceed S$10.0 million and may be less," it added.
The company said its statement on March 21 that it expected second half profits to recover after a first half plunge into the red, was superceded by the new development.
Ipco said it had made a net loss of S$14.75 million in the six months to December 31 1996 against a S$1.02 million profit in the same period in 1995.
